title: Untwine prefetch graph and slim schedule pipeline
creator: Asha Patel
description: Background: Over time the continuous-batching runtime has accreted a tightly coupled prefetch graph that mixes priority logic, task fanout, and kvcache priming. This coupling increases tail latency in corner cases (bursty short sessions) and makes scheduler changes risky. Goal: Separate the prefetch/priming graph from the scheduling control plane, simplify the per-session state machine, and remove redundant buffering paths so we can safely apply next-quarter scheduler heuristics and reduce memory churn. This ticket focuses on the refactor and measurement scaffolding; performance tuning follow-ups will be separate.
acceptance_criteria: Unit and integration tests covering new prefetch graph boundaries (>=90% of modified modules)
End-to-end benchmarks show no regression on p50/p90 latency for common workloads (within 5%), and p99 tail improved or unchanged
KV priming latency variance reduced by >=20% on synthetic hotkey replay benchmark
Scheduler path no longer reads or mutates prefetch-specific state (code boundaries enforced by linter rule)
Rollout plan validated in canary cluster with traffic shadowing and automated rollback hooks
tech_notes: Introduce PrefetchProxy interface that owns kvcache priming requests and returns opaque tokens; scheduler only holds tokens (decouples lifecycle)
Replace ad-hoc ring buffers with a single lightweight event stream for prefetch intents to reduce copies; use existing fastqueue library ops
Keep a compatibility shim for legacy adapters for 2 release cycles (runtime-1.x -> runtime-2.0) to avoid breaking Dedicated customers
Trade-offs: extra token indirection adds ~2-5µs in the happy path but enables batch-level coalescing and safer lifecycle handling; acceptable given overall tail reduction
Dependency upgrades: bump fastqueue from 1.6.2 -> 2.0.0 (breaking API), and kernel-selectors to 3.1.0 for new affinity hints. Tests and migration shims included.
rollout_plan: Implement behind feature flag 'prefetch_isolation_v2'. Merge behind flag, run CI and internal performance CI. Deploy to canary region (us-west-2) at 5% of serving nodes with traffic shadowing for 48h. If metrics (p99 latency, kv-priming-failures, CPU spend) stable, increase to 25% for 24h then to 100%. Use automatic rollback on >=3% p99 regression or >=0.2% increase in kv-priming timeouts. Coordinate with Dedicated ops for scheduled upgrade windows and include notes for customers in release notes.
testing_notes: New microbench: prefetch-token-latency (runs in perf CI); baseline attached in Confluence page
Add end-to-end smoke test that asserts session creation -> prefetch token issuance -> kvcache fill succeeds within 50ms in unit CI
Manual QA: run sampled customer queries in staging with shadowing for 6 hours and check output parity and token-level cost
